by all threads in the warpgroup prior to reaching the fence.

head_commit.message:
Mark MultiProcessGpuTest multiaccelerator and require 4 GPUs for MPI tests.

The Open MPI and mpi4py tests start 4 MPI ranks, and each rank uses
the GPU that matches its local rank. In the single accelerator pytest
pass, xdist pins each worker to one GPU, so ranks 1-3 fail and rank 0
times out waiting for their topology. Mark the class multiaccelerator
so these tests run in the multiaccelerator pass, and skip the MPI
tests when fewer than 4 GPUs are visible, using the same check as
`test_gpu_distributed_initialize`.

display_title: jax.scipy.fft: add dst, dstn, idst and idstn (type 2)

head_commit.message:
jax.scipy.fft: add dst, dstn, idst and idstn (type 2)

Add the type 2 discrete sine transform and its inverse to jax.scipy.fft,
following the scipy.fft API:

- dst and idst are the 1-D transforms. They use the identity
  DST-II(x)[k] = DCT-II((-1)**n * x)[N - 1 - k], so each one is a sign flip,
  the corresponding dct/idct and a reversal, and inherits the rfft/irfft
  based implementation of the cosine transforms.
- dstn and idstn are the n-dimensional transforms, built the same way on
  dctn and idctn instead of looping over the 1-D functions.

As for the cosine transforms, only type 2 is implemented and other types
raise NotImplementedError; norm accepts None, "backward" and "ortho".

Three private helpers are added. _dst_sign multiplies by (-1)**n along the
given axes using an iota, so no size-dependent constant is embedded in the
compiled program. _dctn_s_axes normalizes the s and axes arguments and
_pad_axes zero-pads or truncates several axes in a single lax.pad. The last
two replace the equivalent inline code in dct, dctn, idct and idctn, whose
behavior is unchanged.

The tests share the existing dct parameterization: each sampled case runs
the cosine and the sine variant in a subTest, so the cosine coverage is
unchanged when a single case is generated.

Co-authored-by: Chris Ninham <61634310+Nin17@users.noreply.github.com>

display_title: Strip device assignment in CPU cache keys

head_commit.message:
Strip device assignment in CPU cache keys

`cache_key.get` currently strips `device_assignment` from serialized `CompileOptions` only on GPU. In multi-process CPU jobs, process-local `jit` calls carry each worker's global device ID in `device_assignment` (`[[0]]` on process 0 vs. `[[2048]]` on process 1). Since XLA:CPU compilation does not depend on `device_assignment`, non-zero processes miss persistent cache entries written by process 0 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So let's strip `device_assignment` when hashing `CompileOptions` on CPU as well, matching GPU.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025316908

display_title: Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 970283402

head_commit.message:
Add `is_async` option to `compute_on` for async SparseCore offload.

Lower `compute_on(..., compute_type='tpu_sparsecore', is_async=True)` to an
async `@"compute-on-start"` custom call returning `core.AbstractFuture`
outputs materialized via `.done()` (`compute_on_done_p` ->
`@"compute-on-done"`):

- Drop the `shard_map` wrapper around `compute_on_done` and rely on native
  Shardy/GSPMD propagation across the async pair.
- Fix `sdy.sharding_constraint` emission via `mlir.lower_with_sharding_in_types`
  on both `@"compute-on-start"` (unwrapped `out_avals`) and
  `@"compute-on-done"`, also enabling Auto mode and HiJAX `unreduced` inputs.
- Default empty `sparse_core_config` in lowering when async and
  `compiler_options` is omitted or `{}`.
- Add explicit `NotImplementedError` guards for unsupported `is_async=True`
  transforms and options (`vmap`, `jvp`, `linearize`/`vjp`/`grad`, partial
  evaluation / `remat`, `transpose`, eager mode, non-`Device` outputs,
  non-single outputs, high-level outputs, and non-`tpu_sparsecore`
  `compute_type`).
- Add lowering, DCE, error-guard, and TPU overlap tests in `overlap_test.py`
  (deferring loop-carried futures across `jax.lax.scan`).

display_title: Avoid redundant PRNG work in `jax.random.gumbel` (`mode="highest"`).

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant PRNG work in `jax.random.gumbel` (`mode="highest"`).

In `float32` `mode="highest"`, the `threefry2x32` PRNG work in `_gumbel` was duplicated since `threefry2x32` already outputs two `uint32` words per hash, but `_random_bits(..., shape=(2,) + shape)` collapsed each pair into one word and ran twice as many hashes.

Fix this by drawing `(hi, lo)` directly as two `*shape` streams via `prng.random_bits(..., num_streams=2)` and hoisting `-jnp.log` out of `jnp.where` to make it easier for XLA to fuse ops while avoiding duplicate PRNG work.

Also, gate the `num_streams=2` path to multi-stream PRNGs (`num_streams >= 2`, i.e., `threefry2x32`, `threefry4x32`, `philox`), and update legacy `threefry2x32.threefry_raw_bits` (`threefry_partitionable=False`) to use a single `(2, *shape)` pass so legacy `gumbel` streams stay bitwise identical and other `num_streams=2` callers avoid a split plus two passes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1023281056

Fetch executable local devices lazily for effect runtime tokens.

Creating a replicated execution wrapper previously queried and wrapped

Register shard_map_collective_rule for relayout_p in pjit.

Without a `shard_map_collective_rule`, lowering `relayout_p` under `jax_partitioning=True` on an explicit mesh raises `NotImplementedError`. Both `explicit_layout` and `relayout` bind `relayout_p`, so explicit-mesh functions using layouts fail to lower.

name: CI - Wheel Tests (Continuous)
display_title: Fix hyp1f1 values and gradients for negative x

head_commit.message:
Fix hyp1f1 for negative x

For -100 < x < 0 hyp1f1 summed the Taylor series directly, whose terms
alternate in sign and cancel, and for x <= -100 it used the asymptotic
expansion for large positive x. Both gave wrong results, e.g.
hyp1f1(0.5, 1.5, -50) returned -381 instead of 0.1253.

For x < 0, use Kummer's transformation
1F1(a, b, x) = exp(x) 1F1(b - a, b, -x). For x > -100 the series of
1F1(b - a, b, -x) is summed with exp(x / 2) applied to its terms and to
the sum, so that it does not overflow in float32. For x <= -100 the
asymptotic expansion of 1F1(b - a, b, -x) is used with exp(x) cancelled
out.

Also:
- Truncate the divergent asymptotic series at their smallest term
  instead of summing growing terms up to k = 250, and combine their
  gamma, exp and power factors in log space so that they do not overflow
  separately in float32.
- Use the terminating series for any x when a is a non-positive integer,
  where the expansion for large x divides by gamma(a) and gave nan, and
  stop the series where it terminates, which gave nan for a negative
  integer b.
- Compute the derivatives with respect to a and b by differentiating the
  recurrence between the terms of the series, and for |x| >= 100 by
  differentiating the asymptotic expansions (d/da was wrong by a factor
  of 600 at x = 300).

The tests compare against scipy.special.hyp1f1 on a grid of negative x
on both sides of x = -100, against closed forms of 1F1 (exp, expm1, erf
and a terminating polynomial), and against mpmath values of the
derivatives in a and b.

Fixes #21503

display_title: [monitoring] Make `clear_event_listeners()` also clear scalar listeners.

head_commit.message:
[monitoring] Make `clear_event_listeners()` also clear scalar listeners.

Code that resets JAX monitoring with the public
`jax.monitoring.clear_event_listeners()` keeps every listener added with
`jax.monitoring.register_scalar_listener()`. Those listeners keep firing on
later `record_scalar` calls. For example, a training library that registers a
scalar listener for a metrics backend and calls `clear_event_listeners()` on
shutdown still has the stale listener called on the next compile:

```python
calls = []
jax.monitoring.register_scalar_listener(lambda *a, **k: calls.append(a))
jax.monitoring.clear_event_listeners()
jax.monitoring.record_scalar("/test/scalar", 1.0)
assert not calls  # Fails before this change: len(calls) == 1.
```

Root cause: `clear_event_listeners()` assigns `_scalar_listeners = []`, but
`_scalar_listeners` is missing from the function's `global` statement. The
assignment binds a local name and the module-level list is unchanged. The other
three listener lists are already declared `global` and are cleared.

Fix: declare `_scalar_listeners` global too, like the other listener lists.

Added `test_clear_event_listeners_clears_scalar_listeners` to
`tests/monitoring_test.py`. It registers a scalar listener, calls
`clear_event_listeners()`, records a scalar, and checks that the listener was
not called and that no scalar listeners remain. It fails before the fix and
passes after.

name: CI - Wheel Tests (Continuous)
display_title: [multihost_utils] Group devices by process in `process_allgather` and `broadcast_one_to_all`.

head_commit.message:
[multihost_utils] Group devices by process in `process_allgather` and `broadcast_one_to_all`.

On multi-host TPU slices where `jax.devices()` is not grouped by
`process_index`, `multihost_utils.process_allgather` (and `assert_equal` /
`sync_global_devices`, which call it) returns wrong results, and
`broadcast_one_to_all` raises:

```
ValueError: When passing host local inputs to pjit, devices connected to a
single host must form a contiguous subcube of the global device mesh
```

For example, on a 128-host ICI-resilient TPU slice, 63 of the 128 processes got
a different `process_allgather` result from the other 65, with no error.

Root cause: both functions build their `('processes', 'local_devices')` mesh as
`np.array(jax.devices()).reshape(process_count, local_device_count)`. This
assumes row `p` holds exactly process `p`'s devices. But `jax.devices()` is
sorted by global device id, not by `process_index`, so that is not always true.
If the process blocks are permuted, `out[p]` holds another process's data. If
the processes' devices are interleaved, the mesh mixes hosts within a row.

Fix: add a small `_devices_by_process()` helper that stable-sorts
`jax.devices()` by `process_index` before the reshape, and use it in both
places. Like `mesh_utils.create_hybrid_device_mesh(process_is_granule=True)`,
it groups devices by `process_index`. Because the sort is stable, the mesh is
unchanged whenever `jax.devices()` is already grouped by process, which is the
case for all topologies that work today.

Tested: added `test_devices_not_grouped_by_process` to the multiprocess
`multihost_utils_test`. It patches `jax.devices()` to return (a) the processes
in reverse order and (b) the processes' devices interleaved. It then checks
that `process_allgather(process_index)[p] == p`, that `broadcast_one_to_all`
returns process 0's value, and that `sync_global_devices` succeeds. Before this
fix, (a) returned `[3, 2, 1, 0]` instead of `[0, 1, 2, 3]` and (b) raised the
`ValueError` above.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026565904

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

display_title: Avoid materializing device arrays when concretizing abstract meshes.

head_commit.message:
Avoid materializing device arrays when concretizing abstract meshes.

Concretizing an AbstractMesh previously built a NumPy object array of
every device, flattened it back into a tuple, and constructed a duplicate
DeviceList before looking up the Mesh in the interning table. On large
meshes, that paid linear Python work under the GIL on every new device
subset even when the concrete Mesh had already been created and interned.

Key Mesh interning directly on the axis sizes and DeviceList,
materializing the NumPy device array only when no matching Mesh is
already interned.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] [pallas:sc] Fix WAR data race in `VectorSubcoreTest.test_barrier`

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] [pallas:sc] Fix WAR data race in `VectorSubcoreTest.test_barrier`

After the first `plsc.subcore_barrier()`, each subcore copies `o_ref[(subcore_id + 1) % mesh.num_subcores]` into its private VMEM and then immediately overwrites `o_ref[subcore_id]` in HBM without an intervening barrier. If subcore `s + 1` reads `o_ref[s + 2]` and writes back to `o_ref[s + 1]` before subcore `s` finishes reading `o_ref[s + 1]`, subcore `s` observes `2 * (s + 2)` instead of `2 * (s + 1)`.

Add a second `plsc.subcore_barrier()` between reading the neighbor's slice from `o_ref` and writing the updated slice back to `o_ref`.

display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Support TF32 MMAs with K-fastest operands on Blackwell.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support TF32 MMAs with K-fastest operands on Blackwell.

`tcgen05.mma` accepted float32 operands, but could not issue them: the
instruction descriptor had no encoding for TF32, and `.kind::tf32` was missing.
It now issues `tcgen05.mma.kind::tf32` for float32 A (in SMEM or TMEM) and B,
with float32 accumulators.

The MMA truncates the float32 mantissas of its operands to the 10 bits of TF32
rather than rounding them, unlike XLA's TF32 matmuls, which round to nearest
even. Callers that want XLA's results must round the operands first, e.g. with
`jax.lax.reduce_precision`.

M- or N-fastest TF32 operands need the 128B swizzle with 32B atoms, which Mosaic
GPU does not support. With the other swizzles, the MMA leaves the accumulator
unchanged (zeros in the tests), so `tcgen05.mma` raises `NotImplementedError`
for them instead.
